issue.title: sase-core flake: sudo_runner cwd_removed_after_authentication_fails_before_dispatch_and_cleans_up leaves the cwd behind under load
issue.description:
Proposed by epic phase sase-157.9 (sase-core macOS portability epic) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; filed by the sase-157 land agent. Not attributed to sase-157: the test body and its Fixture flow predate the epic (on Linux the Fixture already took the detached path before sase-157.4 made it explicit), and the failure has not been reproduced.

Repo: sase-core. Test: `crates/sase_gateway/src/sudo_runner/tests/dispatch.rs` `cwd_removed_after_authentication_fails_before_dispatch_and_cleans_up` (~line 348).

Observation (sase-157.9 note, 2026-09-21): failed once on the `assert!(!cwd.exists())` assertion across repeated Linux `just check` runs under parallel load, and passed on rerun.

The test writes a `remove_cwd_on_probe` marker so the stub sudo removes the manifest cwd during the authentication probe, then expects a RunnerError, a removed cwd, a Skipped ledger entry, and sudo calls `-k, -v, -n -v, -k`. A surviving cwd suggests the stub's removal step did not run, ran against a different path form, or raced with the runner. The root cause is not yet known: reproduce under load first and capture the ledger/calls when the assertion fails.

The sase-core macOS CI leg is now required (sase-157.9), so this flake can turn master red on either platform.

task_type_fields.evidence: 1 failure (`!cwd.exists()` assertion) across repeated Linux `just check` runs under full parallel load; passed on rerun of the unchanged tree. Not reproduced serially; ledger and sudo-call trace were not captured. Reported by sase-157.9.
